newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: OPG sees breakthrough in Germany.
newsitem.headline: OPG sees breakthrough in Germany.

text.p: Dutch drugs wholesaler and producer OPG said on Tuesday Sanacorp of Germany had agreed to promote some of OPG's generic (non-branded) drugs there.

"For the first time in its existence Sanacorp has said that it is prepared to give up its neutral stance on products and distribute ours with a bigger effort," OPG board member Robert Peek told a news conference.
"That is a sign of hope and one that the IPSO cooperation (between major drugs wholesalers in Europe) is paying off," he said, adding that Germany was by far Europe's biggest pharmaceuticals market.

"If you asked us six months ago whether IPSO was working, we would have been quite pessimistic. But it does work on a one-to-one basis in which partners find each other on specific deals," said OPG chairman John Blom.
OPG would also continue its efforts to market a broad range of generic, patent-free drugs in other European countries such as Denmark and Belgium through its sales offices there.
OPG aims to become a worldwide player with its generic anti-asthma and cancer drugs. "We have a strong position there, but in order to survive we have to become an international player," Peek said.
OPG would therefore launch a number of new important drugs in the United States in the coming years, he said.
The Dutch company recently introduced three generic products in the U.S., but now wanted to lead the market.
"We expect to be the first in the U.S. to introduce the generic variant of these drugs (one of which is Tamoxifen). "We are very satisfied with our pipeline and partner," Peek said.
Blom said that a quick market entry with generic drugs was vital to the firm's success, market share and profitability.
Fifty percent of the world's cancer and asthma drugs are sold in the U.S., Blom said.

OPG declined to detail the contribution of generic drugs as a percentage of turnover, but its pharmaceutical business -- which also includes parallel drugs import and raw materials -- generated 470 million guilders, or 17 percent of total sales, in the 1995/1996 bookyear.

The company said it expected its services and drugs production arms to generate an increasing share of profits as profit margins in its core wholesale activities, 81 percent of sales, were hurt by a recent Dutch price law.
